def: In front of the orbital septum, the eyelid membrane. Preseptal cellulitis infects the eyelid without affecting eye movement or vision, unlike orbital cellulitis.
The narrow bone segment between the superior and inferior articular facets of a vertebra. A defect there (spondylolysis) can allow forward slippage of the vertebra (spondylolisthesis).
Surgical incision through burned, leathery skin (eschar) to relieve pressure from swelling, performed for circumferential burns that threaten limb circulation or breathing.
Surgical ligation of the dilated pampiniform plexus veins of a varicocele, done for pain, infertility or testicular atrophy.
A branch of the subclavian artery that gives off the inferior thyroid, suprascapular and transverse cervical arteries. Ligation of the inferior thyroid artery risks recurrent laryngeal nerve injury.
Producing bright echoes on ultrasound, appearing white because the tissue reflects sound well, such as retained placental tissue or bone.
Slower-than-expected progress of labor, such as protracted dilation or descent in the active phase, often from inadequate contractions, a large fetus or maternal obesity.
Describing a nonstress test with fewer than two accelerations of fetal heart rate in 20 minutes, requiring further testing like a biophysical profile.
Sound and vibration applied to the maternal abdomen to wake a sleeping fetus and provoke fetal heart rate accelerations during a nonreactive nonstress test.
Small valveless veins passing through skull foramina connecting scalp and dural venous sinuses. Infection can spread intracranially through them.
The resting phase of the hair growth cycle when hair stops growing and eventually sheds. Telogen effluvium is diffuse shedding after stress.
Redistribution of pulmonary blood flow to the upper lung zones, seen as prominent upper-lobe veins on chest x-ray in pulmonary venous hypertension from heart failure.
The sharp angle on a chest x-ray where the diaphragm meets the chest wall. Blunting of it indicates pleural fluid of around 200 mL or more.
Relating to cryoglobulins, immunoglobulins that precipitate in the cold. Cryoglobulinemic vasculitis causes purpura, arthralgia and glomerulonephritis, associated with hepatitis C.
The ethical principle that physicians should act in the patient's best interest and do good.
The ethical principle of "first, do no harm"; avoiding actions that injure patients.
Relating to the urinary bladder, as in superior and inferior vesical arteries.
Using continuous real-time x-ray imaging, such as sniff tests of diaphragm movement for phrenic nerve injury or barium swallows.
Persistent, painful sensation of needing to defecate even when the rectum is empty, caused by rectal inflammation or tumors.
Ultrasound of the uterus with saline instilled in the cavity to detect polyps, fibroids or adhesions.
Having leaked out of a vessel into surrounding tissue, as blood or contrast agents or IV drugs.
Brand of progestin-releasing subdermal contraceptive implant (etonogestrel) lasting about 3 years.
A condition with many pustules, small pus-filled skin blisters, such as acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis.
Excessively loud, low-pitched sound on chest percussion, indicating trapped air as in pneumothorax or emphysema.
Containing many compartments, as with a multilocular ovarian cyst, which has septations and may suggest a mucinous tumor.
Rod-shaped gram-positive bacteria that normally dominate vaginal flora and keep pH acidic. Their loss contributes to bacterial vaginosis.
Brighter than surrounding tissue on ultrasound. Dermoid cysts of the ovary often appear hyperechoic.
Drugs that prevent platelet aggregation, such as aspirin and clopidogrel, used in arterial thrombosis prevention.
Within the amniotic sac. Intraamniotic infection (chorioamnionitis) presents with maternal fever, uterine tenderness and fetal tachycardia.
Describing a fracture whose bone ends remain properly aligned, often treated without surgery.
Hazy increase in lung density on CT that preserves vessel margins, seen in interstitial lung disease, organizing pneumonia and viral pneumonia.
Beneath the galea aponeurotica of the scalp. Neonatal subgaleal hemorrhage can be large and life-threatening.
Removal of excess amniotic fluid by needle in polyhydramnios, for example in twin-twin transfusion syndrome.
Beneath the chorion; a subchorionic hematoma is a first-trimester bleed between the uterus and chorionic membrane.
Warts, rough skin growths from HPV. Verruca vulgaris is common; genital warts (condylomata) are from types 6 and 11.
Inflammation of the liver capsule, as in Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome from gonococcal or chlamydial PID, producing violin-string adhesions.
Kissing or triatomine bug that transmits Trypanosoma cruzi, the cause of Chagas disease.
Obligate intracellular bacteria of the genus Chlamydia.
Brand name for carboprost, a prostaglandin F2-alpha analog used for postpartum hemorrhage from uterine atony. Contraindicated in asthma.
Initiation of milk production by the breast, driven by prolactin after delivery as estrogen and progesterone fall.
Stable peptide cleaved from vasopressin's precursor, a marker of ADH release.
Anion that competitively inhibits sodium-iodide symporter in the thyroid, blocking iodide uptake.
Removal of iodine from molecules, such as T4 to T3 conversion by deiodinases or recycling of iodine from MIT and DIT.
Promoting growth and function of a target tissue. TSH has a trophic effect on the thyroid.
Protein induced by glucocorticoids that inhibits phospholipase A2, reducing arachidonic acid release.
Aldosterone-secreting adrenal adenoma, the commonest cause of primary hyperaldosteronism (Conn syndrome).
Initial insulin precursor with a signal peptide, cleaved in ER to proinsulin.
Blood pH above 7.45. Lowers free ionized calcium by increasing albumin binding.
Promoting urinary phosphate excretion, as PTH and FGF23 do.
Growth hormone receptor antagonist used for acromegaly refractory to surgery; IGF-1 monitored.
Heat production, increased by thyroid hormone raising metabolic rate.
Spontaneous loss of a body part from ischemia or infection, as in diabetic foot gangrene.
Hypertension and hypokalemia mimicking excess aldosterone without high aldosterone, e.g., licorice ingestion or Liddle syndrome.
Diffuse overgrowth of ganglion cells and nerves in the gut wall, seen with MEN 2B.
Rapid-acting insulin analog with onset in minutes.
Class of diabetes drugs (pioglitazone, rosiglitazone) activating PPAR-gamma to improve insulin sensitivity.
SGLT2 inhibitor for type 2 diabetes and heart failure; causes glucosuria, genital infections.
SGLT2 inhibitor for type 2 diabetes with cardiovascular and renal benefit.
Mid-cycle one-sided lower abdominal pain around ovulation, from follicular rupture.
Onset of pubic hair, from adrenal androgens (Tanner stage II).
Transition period before menopause with irregular cycles and symptoms.
Malignant skeletal muscle precursor cell in rhabdomyosarcoma, with cross-striations.
